docs.text: Transport and Protocol Wire layer under gameplay netcode and collaboration: TCP sockets, 4-byte big-endian length prefix + msgpack frames, typed messages, per-frame drain. Gameplay transport ( core/network/transp/ , singleton via get_transport() ) API Signature / meaning host host(host="0.0.0.0", port=7777, max_players=16) -> bool — starts GameServer in a thread, resets role to server, local_id = 0 connect connect(host="127.0.0.1", port=7777, name="Player") -> bool — starts GameClient , sends JOIN {"name"} , waits up to 5 s, returns False on NET_KICK disconnect disconnect() — stops client/server, clears the queue, role back to "none" send send(msg_type, data) — client → server; on server role acts as broadcast send_to send_to(peer_id, msg_type, data) — server → one peer; on client role falls back to send to server broadcast broadcast(msg_type, data) — alias of send (server fans out to all peers) poll poll() -> list[(msg_type, data)] — drain incoming without blocking; call every frame peek / get_peers peek() non-destructive read; get_peers() -> [{id, name}] on server State is_connected , is_server , is_client , local_id (server 0 , client = assigned peer id), peer_count , bytes_sent , bytes_received Caps / callbacks set_max_players(n) lives on GameServer , not on Transport ; set_on_connected / set_on_disconnected live on GameClient , not on Transport Protocol ( core/network/protocol.py , core/config/constants.py ) Framing: make_msg(msg_type, data) packs msgpack {"t": int, "d": dict} with a ">I" length prefix; FRAME_HEADER_SIZE = 4 ; payloads over MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE (4 MiB) raise instead of sending; parse_msg is the inverse. MessageType IntEnum: gameplay range NET_SPAWN = 100 , NET_DESPAWN = 101 , NET_SPAWN_REQUEST = 102 , NET_RPC = 103 , NET_TRANSFORM = 104 , NET_RIGIDBODY = 105 , NET_ANIMATOR = 106 , NET_OWNER_CHANGE = 107 , NET_VARIABLES = 108 , NET_READY = 109 , NET_KICK = 110 , NET_SNAPSHOT = 111 (collaboration types occupy 1–55, 210–212). RPC shapes: plugin events travel as NET_RPC {"rpc": name, "payload": {...}} with the server stamping _sender before dispatch; component calls travel as NET_RPC {"net_id", "method", "args", "rpc_type", "target?"} via rpc.send_server_rpc / send_client_rpc / send_target_rpc . Collaboration transport (separate path, do not confuse) CollabServer ( core/network/serverp/base.py , connection.py ): set_password / set_room / set_max_clients , _auth_ok (room + token check), update_scene_data . CollabClient ( core/network/client.py ): connect(host, port, name, password, room) , set_on_auth_failed . Relay ( core/network/relayp/ ) and UPnP ( core/network/upnpp/ ) helpers serve this path. Gameplay GameServer has none of that: first frame must be JOIN , over-capacity peers get NET_KICK {"reason": "server_full"} and the socket closes. Limits TCP only — asyncio.start_server / asyncio.open_connection with TCP_NODELAY , so high-rate state pays head-of-line blocking; no UDP channel, no encryption, no gameplay-side auth. The server relays only transform/rigidbody/animator/variables/RPC/snapshot to other peers; spawn requests, ownership changes and despawns are consumed by NetworkManager . Transport.send on a server broadcasts — targeted delivery needs send_to ; a client cannot unicast, it always sends to the server. NetworkPlugin.poll() and NetworkManager.on_update() drain the same singleton deque, so run one pump per frame (the manager forwards NET_RPC {"rpc": ...} frames to the plugin). Usage: host() once on the host machine, connect() on joiners, then poll() every frame and dispatch by MessageType . Keep payloads flat and tiny (ids, positions, enums); large transfers go through split_chunks ( CHUNK ) or snapshots, never per-frame whole scenes. Troubleshooting: connect refused → server not started or port blocked/firewalled; kicked at join → server_full ; silent peers → poll() not called each frame or two pumps fighting over one queue; oversize send → ValueError , split the payload. Related: Network Plugin (gameplay wiring), NetworkManager (session component), Collaboration (editor sessions), RPC usage in NetworkManager.send_rpc . Verified against: core/network/transp/transport.py:39-80,82-157 ; core/network/transp/server.py:59-66,108-124,140-160,223-263,269-317 ; core/network/transp/client.py:52-64,91-129,148-186 ; core/network/protocol.py:26-111,147-163 ; core/network/rpc.py:72-105 ; core/config/constants.py:20-21 ; core/network/serverp/base.py:80-87,174-189,233-234 ; core/components/network/netmgr/manager.py:124-172 .

docs.text: Physics 2D Overview Planar dynamics with its own components ( Rigidbody2D , BoxCollider2D , CircleCollider2D ), simulated by the same solver but flagged 2D: out-of-plane velocity and tilt are zeroed every step so bodies never drift off-plane. docs.text: Box Collider Axis-aligned box shape in local space. The cheapest shape in any solver — crates, walls, floors, triggers, buttons. Properties Field Default Notes layer 0 Collision layer index, 0–15 mask 0xFFFF Collide-with bitmask center (0, 0, 0) Local offset, scaled by Transform scale ( scaled_center ) size (1, 1, 1) Full extents, scaled by Transform scale ( scaled_size ) is_trigger False Reports overlaps, no contact response physic_material "" .zphysmat asset path; wins over inline values when set material_friction 0.6 Inline fallback material_bounciness 0.0 Inline fallback Usage in Editor Set Size / Center , pick Layer + Collision Mask , tick Is Trigger for sensors. Multiple BoxCollider components allowed per entity (compound). Usage in Code entity = scene.create_entity("Crate") from core.components.physics.rigidbody import Rigidbody from core.components.physics.box_collider import BoxCollider from core.maths.math3d import Vec3 rb = Rigidbody() rb.mass = 1.0 entity.add_component(rb) box = BoxCollider() box.size = Vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) box.center = Vec3(0.0, 0.5, 0.0) box.is_trigger = False box.layer = 0 box.mask = 0xFFFF entity.add_component(box) def on_fixed_update(self, dt): rb = self._entity.get_component(Rigidbody) if rb is not None: rb.add_force(Vec3(5.0, 0.0, 0.0)) def on_collision_enter(self, other_id, force=0.0): pass Fixed update notes Shape key ( size , center , friction, restitution, trigger) is re-checked every 60 physics steps ( _shape_check_counter ); changed shapes rebuild the body ( rebuild_entity ). Solver call: create_rigid_body(shape_type="box", shape_params={"size", "center"}) ; bodies with several primitive shapes merge via create_compound_rigid_body . dt is Engine._fixed_dt ( 0.02 default). docs.text: Buoyancy Floating bodies for ponds, rivers and oceans: hulls displace water, waves rock them, currents push them. CPU sampling in on_fixed_update — not a solver body. Properties Field Default Notes density 500.0 Inspector 1–20000 ; object density volume 0.0 Override; 0 = auto from collider (box sx*sy*sz , sphere 4/3πr³ , capsule 4/3πr³ + πr²h ) water_density 1000.0 Inspector 1–2000 linear_drag 8.0 Inspector 0–50 (deserialize fallback 1.5 ) angular_drag 6.0 Inspector 0–50 (deserialize fallback 1.2 ) flow_influence 1.0 Inspector 0–10 use_waves / use_flow True / True Sample height_at / flow_at from WaterVolume sample_resolution 8 Inspector 2–24 grid per axis max_acceleration 8.0 × g clamp on net acceleration enable_debug False Fills gizmo_lines with sample points Read-only submerged_fraction 0–1 displaced/total volume Usage in Editor Add Rigidbody (non-kinematic) + Box / Sphere / CapsuleCollider + Buoyancy , place a WaterVolume in the scene. Tune density vs water_density , linear_drag for hull feel. Usage in Code entity = scene.create_entity("Boat") from core.components.physics.rigidbody import Rigidbody from core.components.physics.box_collider import BoxCollider from core.components.physics.buoyancy import Buoyancy rb = Rigidbody() rb.mass = 500.0 entity.add_component(rb) box = BoxCollider() entity.add_component(box) b = Buoyancy() b.density = 500.0 b.linear_drag = 8.0 b.sample_resolution = 8 entity.add_component(b) def on_fixed_update(self, dt): # Buoyancy.on_fixed_update runs itself: Archimedes + quadratic/viscous # drag + flow-relative velocity, clamped to max_acceleration * 9.81. frac = b.submerged_fraction Requires a collider shape (build fails without one) and at least one WaterVolume entity, else submerged_fraction stays 0 . Fixed update notes Runs in component on_fixed_update(dt) with dt = Engine._fixed_dt ( 0.02 default); force path is rb.add_force / rb.add_torque , applied on the next physics push. Skipped when kinematic or Transform-less. Gravity magnitude used internally: _GRAVITY_MAG = 9.81 . Related Rigidbody, Box/Sphere/Capsule colliders, WaterVolume (environment), Solver & Threading. docs.text: Collision Layers Who collides with whom, independent of surface response. Every collider carries layer (default 0 ) and mask (default 0xFFFF ); contact requires both sides to accept each other. Properties Field Default Notes MAX_LAYERS 16 Layers 0–15 layer 0 Per-collider index mask 0xFFFF Per-c Collider bitmask Default names Default, TransparentFX, Ignore Raycast, Water, UI, Player, Enemy, Projectile, Trigger, Ground, Layer10–15 DEFAULT_LAYER_NAMES Default matrix All-vs-all except exclusions build_default_collision_matrix() : layer 2 (Ignore Raycast) collides with nothing; layer 4 (UI) collides only with itself Usage in Editor Set Layer + Collision Mask on each collider. Typical plan: 0 World (everything), 5 Player, 6 Enemy (mute enemy-vs-enemy for crowds), 7 Projectile (world + characters only), 8 Trigger pickups (player only). Usage in Code entity = scene.create_entity("Pickup") from core.components.physics.sphere_collider import SphereCollider s = SphereCollider() s.radius = 1.0 s.is_trigger = True s.layer = 8 s.mask = 1 << 5 # only player layer entity.add_component(s) from core.physics.collision_layers import build_default_collision_matrix, get_layer_mask matrix = build_default_collision_matrix() mask = get_layer_mask([], matrix, 0) def on_collision_enter(self, other_id, force=0.0): pass # triggers report through the same mask test, no contact response Helpers: layer_mask_from_names(names, indices) , layer_names_from_mask(names, mask) . Fixed update notes layer / mask pass into every create_rigid_body / create_compound_rigid_body / soft-body call and are evaluated solver-side per step. per_layer_process mode can additionally isolate layers into on-demand solver processes ( plugin._get_layer_process ). Properties Field Default Notes ply_path "" Splat filter *.ply *.sog *.ssog voxel_size 0.25 Inspector 0.02–4.0 opacity_threshold 0.05 Inspector 0–1 dilation 1 Inspector 0–3 max_boxes 2048 Inspector 64–16384 center (0, 0, 0) Local offset added to every box layer / mask 0 / 0xFFFF Filtering is_trigger False Overlap only physic_material "" .zphysmat path material_friction / material_bounciness 0.6 / 0.0 Fallbacks Usage in Editor Assign Splat Path , tune Voxel Size / Opacity Cutoff / Dilation / Max Boxes . Gizmo draws up to 4000 boxes. Usage in Code entity = scene.create_entity("SplatGround") from core.components.physics.gsvol.collider import GSVolumeCollider gs = GSVolumeCollider() gs.ply_path = "assets/capture.ply" gs.voxel_size = 0.25 gs.max_boxes = 2048 entity.add_component(gs) # static: no Rigidbody def on_collision_enter(self, other_id, force=0.0): pass collider_shapes(transform) expands the volume into a list of box shape dicts (size clamped to ≥1e-4 , center includes center offset and Transform scale); empty volumes contribute zero shapes. Requires the cython occupancy/merge helpers — without them volume_boxes() is empty. docs.text: Physics 3D Overview 3D rigid-body simulation in ZarinEngine: entities with a Rigidbody plus one or more colliders are stepped by a pluggable solver ( IPhysicsSolver ), everything else is static scenery. Properties Setting Default Where Solver culverin (Jolt via culverin package) physics_solvers/registry.py DEFAULT_SOLVER , ProjectSettings.json physics.solver Gravity (0.0, -9.81, 0.0) physics.gravity_x/y/z , CulverinSolver._gravity Fixed step 0.02 s engine.fixed_update_dt , physics.fixed_time_step , Engine._fixed_dt Sub-steps 2 physics.num_sub_steps Solver iterations 10 physics.solver_iterations Simulation mode multi_threaded physics.simulation_mode ( single / multi_threaded / per_layer_process ) Usage in Editor Static floor: add BoxCollider only (no Rigidbody ). Dynamic crate: add Rigidbody (mass 1.0 ) + BoxCollider (size 1,1,1 ). Press Play. Kinematic movers: tick is_kinematic and move the Transform; triggers: tick is_trigger and read overlap callbacks. Usage in Code entity = scene.create_entity("Crate") from core.components.physics.rigidbody import Rigidbody from core.components.physics.box_collider import BoxCollider from core.maths.math3d import Vec3 rb = Rigidbody() rb.mass = 1.0 entity.add_component(rb) box = BoxCollider() box.size = Vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) entity.add_component(box) def on_fixed_update(self, dt): rb = self._entity.get_component(Rigidbody) if rb is not None: rb.add_force(Vec3(0.0, 10.0, 0.0)) rb.add_torque(Vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0)) def on_collision_enter(self, other_id, force=0.0): pass # (other_entity_id, impact_force), also on_collision_stay/exit Freeze axes: rb.freeze_pos_x/y/z , rb.freeze_rot_x/y/z (serialized as freeze_pos / freeze_rot triples). Fixed update notes Engine.tick_fixed_step ( core/engine/eng/loop.py ) accumulates real time against _fixed_dt ( 0.02 ), caps the backlog at 5 * _fixed_dt , runs at most 5 steps per tick ( MAX_FIXED_STEPS ), then runs scene.fixed_update(fd) (component on_fixed_update : Buoyancy / Motor / CharacterController forces and drives) and finally system-plugin step(fd) . PhysicsScene.step order: register new entities → shape-change check (every 60 steps) → ECS→physics sync → soft-body AABB separation (only when ≥2 soft bodies) → solver.step_simulation(dt) → 2D constrain → physics→ECS sync → soft sync → collision events. Solver-param scoping: num_sub_steps ( 2 ), solver_iterations ( 10 ), erp ( 0.2 ) are project-config defaults consumed by the PyBullet solver (whose standalone defaults are 1 / 50 / 0.4 ); the default Culverin/Jolt solver ignores them and uses the culverin_* world caps instead. Collision callbacks: script methods accept (other_id) or (other_id, force) — arity auto-detected via inspect.signature ( ScriptComponent._py_collision_arity ); engine-component handlers always receive (other_id, force) . Threading: multi_threaded runs the solver in a daemon multiprocessing.Process ( PhysicsProcess ) over SharedPhysicsBuffer / SoftSharedBuffer ; single runs PhysicsScene in-process (required by CharacterController / Motor ); per_layer_process spawns processes on demand per layer. Related Rigidbody, Box/Sphere/Capsule/Mesh/Terrain/GSVolume colliders, CharacterController, Joints, Motor, Physics Materials, Collision Layers, Solver & Threading, Buoyancy, Soft Body, PhysBone, Constraints (Transform followers — a separate system, not solver joints). Verified against core/physics/scene/scene.py ( step , _register_new_entities , _constrain_2d_bodies ) core/physics/scene/events.py ( _process_collision_events ) core/engine/eng/loop.py ( tick_fixed_step , MAX_FIXED_STEPS = 5 ) core/engine/eng/engine.py ( _fixed_dt = 0.02 ) core/config/config.py ( physics.* defaults) physics_solvers/registry.py ( DEFAULT_SOLVER = "culverin" ) plugins/physics_plug/plugin.py (simulation modes)

Solver-param scoping: num_sub_steps ( 2 ), solver_iterations ( 10 ), erp ( 0.2 ) are project-config defaults consumed by the PyBullet solver (whose standalone defaults are 1 / 50 / 0.4 ); the default Culverin/Jolt solver ignores them and uses the culverin_* world caps instead. Collision callbacks: script methods accept (other_id) or (other_id, force) — arity auto-detected via inspect.signature ( ScriptComponent._py_collision_arity ); engine-component handlers always receive (other_id, force) . Threading: multi_threaded runs the solver in a daemon multiprocessing.Process ( PhysicsProcess ) over SharedPhysicsBuffer / SoftSharedBuffer ; single runs PhysicsScene in-process (required by CharacterController / Motor ); per_layer_process spawns processes on demand per layer.

docs.text: Rigidbody Makes an entity simulated: mass, gravity response, accumulated forces, readable velocities. Without it a collider is static scenery; with it the entity joins the dynamics world. Properties Field Default Notes mass 1.0 Inspector 0.001–100000 ; forced to 0.0 at body creation when is_kinematic drag 0.0 Inspector 0–1000 angular_drag 0.05 Inspector 0–1000 use_gravity True Gravity applies is_kinematic False Transform-driven: pushes dynamics, never pushed freeze_pos_x/y/z False Serialized as freeze_pos triple freeze_rot_x/y/z False Serialized as freeze_rot triple velocity / angular_velocity Vec3.zero() Readable every frame; setter marks body dirty for next sync Usage in Editor Add Rigidbody + one collider ( Box / Sphere / Capsule / Mesh ). Mass 70–90 player-scale, 1–10 crates; keep interacting mass ratios within ~100:1. Tick is_kinematic for movers, freeze rotation axes for non-tipping crates. Usage in Code entity = scene.create_entity("Ball") from core.components.physics.rigidbody import Rigidbody from core.components.physics.sphere_collider import SphereCollider rb = Rigidbody() rb.mass = 2.0 rb.drag = 0.1 rb.freeze_rot_x = True rb.freeze_rot_z = True entity.add_component(rb) col = SphereCollider() col.radius = 0.5 entity.add_component(col) def on_fixed_update(self, dt): rb = self._entity.get_component(Rigidbody) if rb is None or rb.is_kinematic: return rb.add_force(Vec3(0.0, 20.0, 0.0)) # accumulated, cleared after push rb.add_torque(Vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0)) rb.add_impulse(Vec3(0.0, 5.0, 0.0)) # instant velocity change impulse/mass def on_collision_enter(self, other_id, force=0.0): pass def on_collision_stay(self, other_id, force=0.0): pass def on_collision_exit(self, other_id, force=0.0): pass add_force(force, world_space=True) / add_torque(torque) accumulate until the next ECS→physics push, then auto-clear — call every fixed step for continuous thrust. add_impulse is ignored for kinematic bodies and non-positive mass. velocity setter flips _velocity_dirty so the value pushes into the solver on the next sync. Collision callbacks: script on_collision_enter/stay/exit accept (other_id) or (other_id, force) (arity auto-detected via inspect.signature ); engine-component handlers always take (other_id, force) . Fixed update notes dt is Engine._fixed_dt ( 0.02 default); render hitches never change physics dt (backlog capped at 5 * _fixed_dt , max 5 steps/tick). Forces apply in _sync_ecs_to_physics , results ( pos / rot / vel / ang_vel ) come back in _sync_physics_to_ecs ; kinematic and Transform-dirty bodies are skipped on read-back (Transform-driven, never overwritten). In multi_threaded mode this crosses the SharedPhysicsBuffer (flags 1 active, 2 dirty, 4 kinematic/teleport, 8 2D). Related Box/Sphere/Capsule/Mesh colliders, CharacterController, Joints, Solver & Threading, Collision Layers. docs.text: Solver & Threading Where simulation actually runs, and how data crosses the thread/process boundary without gameplay code ever blocking. Properties Setting Default Where simulation_mode multi_threaded single / multi_threaded / per_layer_process solver culverin culverin (Jolt) / pybullet (Bullet) / physx (NVIDIA) fixed_time_step 0.02 Step dt num_sub_steps 2 Project config (PyBullet standalone default 1 ; Culverin/Jolt ignores it) solver_iterations 10 Project config (PyBullet standalone default 50 ; Culverin/Jolt ignores it) erp / contact_erp / friction_erp 0.2 / 0.2 / 0.0 Project config (PyBullet standalone erp / contact_erp default 0.4 ; Culverin/Jolt ignores them) culverin_max_bodies / max_pairs / max_contact_constraints 65536 each Jolt world caps culverin_temp_allocator_size 16777216 16 MB culverin_num_threads / max_jobs / max_barriers 0 / 0 / 0 0 = Jolt single-threaded culverin_penetration_slop 0.02 culverin_enable_ccd / enable_sleeping False / True Shared flags 1 active, 2 dirty, 4 kinematic/teleport, 8 2D SharedPhysicsBuffer Limits 65536 entities, 16 soft bodies × 32768 verts shared_buffer.py , soft_shared_buffer.py Usage in Editor Prototype in default multi_threaded . Switch simulation_mode to single when using CharacterController / Motor or debugging solver behavior; per_layer_process for arenas that must never interact. Usage in Code # Gravity at runtime (IPhysicsSolver API): solver.set_gravity((0.0, -9.81, 0.0)) solver.step_simulation(0.02) solver.apply_force(body_id, (0.0, 10.0, 0.0)) solver.apply_torque(body_id, (0.0, 1.0, 0.0)) solver.apply_impulse(body_id, (0.0, 5.0, 0.0)) hit = solver.ray_cast((0.0, 5.0, 0.0), (0.0, -1.0, 0.0), 100.0) Background step order (verified): coalesce pending step commands into one dt → apply teleports/forces from shared memory → step_simulation(dt) → zero 2D out-of-plane velocity → write back with version bump (+ soft buffers) → map body ids to entity ids for collision events. In-process path mirrors it without serialization: register → shape-check (every 60 steps) → ECS→physics → soft separation (only when ≥2 soft bodies) → step → constrain 2D → physics→ECS → soft sync → events. Fixed update notes Engine.tick_fixed_step : accumulate against _fixed_dt ( 0.02 ), cap backlog 5 * _fixed_dt , max 5 steps/tick, then scene.fixed_update(fd) (component on_fixed_update ) and finally system-plugin step(fd) . PhysicsWorker (threaded fallback): daemon threading.Thread , command poll timeout 0.004 s. SceneThreadPool : max_workers = 2 , ThreadPoolExecutor named phys-scene . docs.text: # Gravity at runtime (IPhysicsSolver API): solver.set_gravity((0.0, -9.81, 0.0)) solver.step_simulation(0.02) solver.apply_force(body_id, (0.0, 10.0, 0.0)) solver.apply_torque(body_id, (0.0, 1.0, 0.0)) solver.apply_impulse(body_id, (0.0, 5.0, 0.0)) hit = solver.ray_cast((0.0, 5.0, 0.0), (0.0, -1.0, 0.0), 100.0) Background step order (verified): coalesce pending step commands into one dt → apply teleports/forces from shared memory → step_simulation(dt) → zero 2D out-of-plane velocity → write back with version bump (+ soft buffers) → map body ids to entity ids for collision events. docs.text: Music, Plotter and QtQuick Smaller bundled extensions for sound, data and UI hosting — same base class, same hooks, narrower jobs. Verified versions: TrackerMusicPlugin 1.0.0 SYSTEM = False , PlotterPlugin 1.2.0 SYSTEM = False , QtQuickWorldPlugin 1.0.0 SYSTEM = True . Tracker Music ( plugins/tracker_music_plugin/ , rend/ engine: engine.py , engine_seq.py , engine_mix.py , engine_fx.py , defs.py ): ProTracker-style module playback (patterns, samples, BPM-relative tempo) for retro scores and demoscene vibes. Drop a module file, drive play/stop from hooks or scripts, mix under positional AudioSources — music bed plus 3D effects is the intended stack. Tempo math follows classic tracker conventions (ticks per row against BPM). Plotter ( plugins/plotter_plugin/ ): Curve and data plotting panels: profiler traces, animation curves, telemetry — see numbers as pictures during tuning. Feed it from step() hooks or log taps; pair with the profiler panel for frame-time forensics. QtQuick ( plugins/qt_quick_plugin/ ): Hosts QtQuick/QML surfaces inside the editor: animated dashboards, custom tool UIs, web-style panels without fighting the widget toolkit. Use for tooling chrome; gameplay UI stays in the GUI system (GuiCanvas widgets ship in builds, QtQuick does not guarantee that). All three iterate like any user plugin (same lifecycle, same config persistence) and package into .zplugin for sharing. Related: Audio System (music bed pairing), Profiler (plotter data source), GUI Overview (gameplay UI home), .zplugin Packaging.

docs.text: Example Plugin Walkthrough plugins/example_plugin.py (43 lines) is the canonical minimal plugin — every convention in one place. Read it, copy it, rename it. from core.foundation.plugins import PluginBase from core.foundation.logger import Logger class ExamplePlugin(PluginBase): NAME = "ExamplePlugin" VERSION = "1.0.0" DESCRIPTION = "Example user plugin demonstrating the plugin API." SYSTEM = False def __init__(self): super().__init__() self._frame = 0 def initialize(self, engine): super().initialize(engine) self.add_menu_item("ExamplePlugin", "Say Hello", lambda: Logger.info("Hello from ExamplePlugin!"), "Ctrl+Shift+H") self.add_toolbar_button("Hello", lambda: Logger.info("Hello from toolbar!"), tooltip="Say hello") Logger.info(f"[{self.NAME}] Initialized! Counter: {self.get_config('counter', 0)}") def on_scene_loaded(self, scene): Logger.debug(f"[{self.NAME}] Scene loaded: {scene.name}") def on_play_start(self): Logger.debug(f"[{self.NAME}] Play started!") self._frame = 0 def on_play_stop(self): Logger.debug(f"[{self.NAME}] Play stopped after {self._frame} frames.") counter = self.get_config("counter", 0) + 1 self.set_config("counter", counter) Logger.info(f"[{self.NAME}] Run counter saved: {counter}") def shutdown(self): Logger.info(f"[{self.NAME}] Shutdown.") def get_plugin(): return ExamplePlugin() Line-by-line lessons: Metadata block ( NAME/VERSION/DESCRIPTION/SYSTEM ) — copy and rename; SYSTEM = False keeps it in the user tier. super().__init__() then super().initialize(engine) — the second call loads the persisted config; without it get_config always returns defaults. add_menu_item(section, label, callback, shortcut) — menu placement with a hotkey; add_toolbar_button(label, callback, tooltip) — one-click access. Callbacks can be lambdas for one-liners. on_scene_loaded(scene) reads scene.name — scene hooks receive the live object, query it directly. on_play_start resets per-run state ( _frame = 0 ); on_play_stop increments and persists the counter — the canonical config round-trip in four lines. shutdown logs; base shutdown (not overridden here beyond logging) saves config and unpatches. Module-level get_plugin() returns a fresh instance — the manager imports the module and calls exactly this. Any name else and the file is invisible. Exercises: change the shortcut and watch the menu update; add step() counting frames into _frame so the stop message reports real numbers; store a second key ( last_scene ) in on_scene_loaded and print it in initialize . Related: PluginBase Lifecycle (all hooks), User Plugins guide (where to put the file), Plugin Manager (how it loads).

docs.text: MCP Bridge Model-Context-Protocol server ( NAME = "ZarinMCP" , VERSION = "2.1.0" , SYSTEM = False in plugins/zarin_mcp/__init__.py ) exposing engine operations to AI agents: scene queries, object creation, property edits, screenshots, code execution — the same surface this documentation workflow drives. Layout in plugins/zarin_mcp/ : mcp_server.py — protocol server: tool registration, request dispatch, response framing. registry.py — tool catalog: every exposed operation registers with name, schema and handler. handlers/ — one module per domain (scene, objects, viewport, execution), keeping the server file thin. main_thread.py — GUI-thread dispatch: document and view mutations must run on the main thread, so background requests marshal through here. mcp_dock.py — editor panel: server status, connected clients, request log, start/stop. Repo roots: zarin_mcp_config.json and zarin_mcp_launcher.py at the project root configure and launch the bridge outside the editor; plugins/mcp_pack-2.1.1.zplugin ships it as a signed distributable (see Packaging). Workflow: launch the bridge (dock or launcher) → connect an MCP-capable agent with the config → the agent lists tools from the registry → scene edits flow as validated operations with screenshots back. Every mutation is an explicit tool call — auditable in the dock log. Safety posture: the bridge can rewrite scenes and run code — bind it to localhost, gate launches behind the dock switch, and review the request log like a sudo history. Troubleshooting: agent cannot connect → server not started or config path wrong; tool missing → registry for that domain not loaded, check the dock; scene edits lag → main-thread queue saturated, lighten the request rate. Related: .zplugin Packaging (the shippable pack), Plugin Manager (load tier), Gizmos (what agents see).

docs.text: Network Plugin (Plugin Page) System plugin ( network_plugin.py , NAME = "NetworkPlugin" , VERSION = "1.0.0" , SYSTEM = True , DESCRIPTION "Multiplayer transport using GameServer/GameClient over TCP") bridging gameplay code and the transport singleton. Plugin-side facts: Loads in the system tier during editor/engine startup; initialize logs readiness, shutdown disconnects cleanly so no session survives quit. Exposes session state as properties: is_connected , is_server , local_id , peer_count — all exception-guarded, safe to poll from UI code. host(port=7777, max_players=16) binds all interfaces; connect(host, port) joins as "Player" ; both log and return bool. Messaging rides MessageType.NET_RPC frames: send(type, payload, target_id) targets one peer from the server or broadcasts otherwise; broadcast(type, payload) always fans out. on_message(type, handler) subscriptions feed NetworkMessage(msg_type, payload, sender_id) ; "*" wildcard catches unhandled traffic for logging. _dispatch_rpc isolates handler exceptions per handler. poll() drains transport frames, dispatches RPC ones, and requeues the remainder back to the transport — non-RPC protocols coexist untouched. handle_transport_messages(msgs) is the seam other systems hook: returns unhandled frames for upstream processing. For the full messaging patterns, payload shapes and session recipes see the Networking section (Transport and Protocol, NetworkManager, Network Plugin usage page) — this page covers the plugin as an engine citizen: where it loads, what it owns, how it shuts down. Troubleshooting (plugin scope): handlers never fire → poll() not pumped or subscribed after traffic started; double handling → same handler subscribed twice (subscriptions append); session survives editor quit → shutdown path bypassed, always disconnect explicitly in tooling. Related: Networking section (protocol, manager, components), Plugin Manager (system tier), PluginBase Lifecycle (hooks used).

docs.text: Plugins Overview Plugins extend the editor and the engine without touching core files: dock panels, toolbar buttons, menu items, new components, file openers, method patches, extra Inspector fields, native extensions. Two flavors: System plugins ( SYSTEM = True , shipped in plugins/ ): physics, network transport, mesh editor, VR, MCP bridge — the engine relies on them, they load first and cannot be casually removed. User plugins ( SYSTEM = False , live in plugins/user/ ): team tools, importers, level utilities, experiment rigs — load after system plugins, enable/disable freely. Three formats, one manager: .py source plugins with a get_plugin() factory returning the instance. Native .dll / .so shared libraries with a Python entry shim. .zplugin signed packages: manifest + code + native modules + bundled libs, verified against config/trusted_keys , extracted once and cached by sha256 fingerprint. PluginManager ( core/foundation/plugins/manager.py ~203 lines, plus base.py / discovery.py / loader.py / lifecycle.py / ui_registry.py ; re-exported by core/foundation/plugins/__init__.py ) owns discovery, _load_order , activation, dependency checks from manifests, security verification, config persistence per plugin, and teardown in reverse order. Pages: PluginBase Lifecycle, Plugin Manager, Example Plugin walkthrough, User Plugins guide, .zplugin Packaging, System Plugins catalog, Network Plugin, VR Plugin, MCP Bridge, Music/Plotter/QtQuick extensions. Five-minute first plugin: copy plugins/example_plugin.py into plugins/user/my_plugin.py , rename the class and NAME , keep get_plugin() at the bottom, restart the editor — the menu item appears, the toolbar button appears, the run counter persists across sessions.

docs.text: Plugin Manager Discovery, ordering, security and teardown for everything pluggable. One class, PluginManager , three plugin tiers: built-in .py , native binaries, signed .zplugin packages. Discovery and order: System plugins load from plugins/ first, user plugins from plugins/user/ after. Registration order appends to _load_order ; teardown walks it in reverse so dependents release before their dependencies. get_system_plugins() filters the tier; iteration helpers yield instances in load order for frames ( step / pre_step ) and event fan-out (scene, play, window hooks). Replacing a plugin (same NAME , new path) swaps the entry in place instead of duplicating — hot iteration without restarts for pure-Python plugins in some flows. Native binaries: .dll / .so entries load through the native path with _native_plugin_path recorded on the instance; a sibling <name>_resources folder auto-resolves as resource_dir . Bundled dependency directories activate per plugin ( _activate_bundled_libs ) so two plugins can ship conflicting library versions without poisoning each other. .zplugin security chain, verified step by step: verify_zplugin_file checks the manifest (name, version, dependencies list with missing-dependency reports), indexes every entry, and rejects unindexed native modules ( _native/ discipline for .pyd / .so / .dll ). Signatures verify against trusted keys from config/trusted_keys (plus an optional configured dir); without keys configured, verification reports "no trusted keys configured" instead of silently passing. _zplugin_fingerprint (sha256 + size + mtime) gates the extraction cache: unchanged packages reuse the extracted tree, changed ones re-extract. Manifest dependencies resolve (including bundled Cython builds via cython_modules ); missing ones log explicitly and block activation. Configuration: per-plugin security knobs ( check_updates_on_startup , trusted_keys_dir ) feed from the plugin security config; per-plugin data persists through the base-class config load/save. Failure posture: a broken plugin logs and skips — one bad apple never prevents editor startup. Check the console first; the plugin manager panel mirrors load state, order and errors. Related: PluginBase Lifecycle, .zplugin Packaging, User Plugins guide, System Plugins catalog.

docs.text: PluginBase Lifecycle Every plugin subclasses PluginBase ( core/foundation/plugins/base.py , re-exported by core/foundation/plugins/__init__.py ) and is constructed through the module-level get_plugin() factory. Metadata first, behavior second. from core.foundation.plugins import PluginBase from core.foundation.logger import Logger class GreetingPlugin(PluginBase): NAME = "GreetingPlugin" VERSION = "1.0.0" DESCRIPTION = "Greets the user and counts Play sessions." SYSTEM = False def __init__(self): super().__init__() self._frame = 0 def initialize(self, engine): super().initialize(engine) self.add_menu_item("GreetingPlugin", "Say Hello", self.hello, "Ctrl+Shift+H") self.add_toolbar_button("Hello", self.hello, tooltip="Say hello") def hello(self): Logger.info("Hello from GreetingPlugin!") def on_play_start(self): self._frame = 0 def on_play_stop(self): total = self.get_config("runs", 0) + 1 self.set_config("runs", total) def shutdown(self): Logger.info("GreetingPlugin shutdown.") def get_plugin(): return GreetingPlugin() Metadata: NAME (manager key and log tag), VERSION , DESCRIPTION , SYSTEM (load tier). The manager keys everything — logs, config files, load order — off NAME , so renames orphan old configs. Lifecycle hooks, in engine order: Hook Signature When initialize (engine) Once at load; always call super() first (loads persisted config) shutdown () At unload; base implementation saves config and restores all patches step (dt) Every frame (scaled time) pre_step (dt) Every fixed step, before scene update on_viewport_ready (viewport) Editor viewport created on_main_window_ready (main_window) Main window assembled — safe to add docks on_project_opened () Project root known on_scene_loaded / on_scene_unloaded (scene) Scene switch boundaries on_play_start / on_play_stop () Session boundaries — reset per-run state here Capabilities (all verified on the base class): UI: add_menu_item(section, label, callback, shortcut) , add_toolbar_button(label, callback, tooltip) ; dock descriptors in self._docks ; file openers in self._file_openers ; new component types in self._components . Patching without forks: patch_component(name, method_patches, extra_inspector_fields, filter_extensions, wraps) , add_inspector_field(component, field) , extend_file_filter(component, field, filter) , patch_function(module, name, wrapper) — everything tracked by a PatchTracker and reverted by unpatch_all() (automatic in base shutdown ). Config: get_config(key, default) / set_config(key, value) persisted per plugin across restarts; engine access via self.engine ; manager via self._manager ; enabled flag for soft on/off. Native side: _native_plugin_path locates the binary; resource_dir resolves the sibling _resources folder; bundled_library_dir exposes shipped dependencies. Rules: never block initialize (defer heavy work to project/scene hooks); always super().initialize(engine) or config never loads; undo every patch you own even though shutdown covers you; gate per-frame work on self.enabled . Related: Plugin Manager, Example Plugin walkthrough, User Plugins guide.

docs.text: System Plugins Catalog Shipped in plugins/ (verified NAME / VERSION / SYSTEM against each get_plugin() file; note: the shipped folder mixes SYSTEM = True engine tier and SYSTEM = False bundled tools — load tier is per-plugin, not per-folder). One page each for the verified two; capsule summaries for the rest. Plugin ( NAME ) Version SYSTEM File(s) ( get_plugin() present) Role NetworkPlugin 1.0.0 True network_plugin.py Gameplay transport wiring: host/connect, message handlers, per-frame poll. See Network Plugin page. PhysicsPlugin 0.4.0 True physics_plug/plugin.py (+ physics_plug/__init__.py re-export) Solver modes (single/multi/per-layer), background process, scene sync. See Solver and Threading. PhysicsVisualisation 1.1.0 True physviz/plugin.py Collision-shape and layer-color debug drawing. QtQuickWorldPlugin 1.0.0 True qt_quick_plugin/plug/plugin.py QtQuick surface hosting inside the editor. VRPlugin 1.0.0 True vr_plugin/plug/plugin.py + vr_plugin/vr_dock.py + vr_plugin/components/ VR runtime core plus editor dock. See VR Plugin page. ZarinMCP 2.1.0 False zarin_mcp/__init__.py (server, dock, registry, handlers) Model-Context-Protocol server exposing engine tools to AI agents. See MCP Bridge page. PlotterPlugin 1.2.0 False plotter_plugin/__init__.py Curve/data plotting panels. TrackerMusicPlugin 1.0.0 False tracker_music_plugin/__init__.py Tracker music playback (rend engine) for retro scores. ExamplePlugin 1.0.0 False example_plugin.py (43 lines) Canonical minimal plugin. See walkthrough. MeshEditorPlugin 1.0.0 False mesh_editor_plugin.py In-editor ProBuilder-style modeling panel and operations. docs.text: User Plugins Guide Team tools live in plugins/user/ as .py files: importers, level utilities, batch renamers, experiment rigs, custom panels. System tier stays untouched; user tier iterates freely. Scaffold, step by step: Copy plugins/example_plugin.py to plugins/user/my_tool.py . Rename the class and NAME (manager key — unique per plugin), bump VERSION , write a one-line DESCRIPTION , keep SYSTEM = False . Implement initialize(engine) : menu items, toolbar buttons, docks, file openers. Defer project-dependent setup to on_project_opened — initialize runs before the project root is known. Add behavior hooks: step for per-frame tools, on_scene_loaded for scene scanners, on_play_start/stop for session rigs. Persist with get_config / set_config — window layouts, last paths, counters survive restarts with zero file code. Restart the editor (or trigger plugin rescan from the manager panel) and verify: menu entry, button, console lines. Patching etiquette: extend components with add_inspector_field and patch_component instead of editing core files — your fields ride engine updates instead of conflicting with them. Everything unpatches on shutdown automatically. Debugging: console first (import errors name the missing module and line), manager panel second (load state per plugin), Logger.debug breadcrumbs third. A plugin that raises in initialize is skipped with a log — the editor always starts. Distribution inside a team: share the .py file directly for trusted colleagues; ship .zplugin for everyone else (signed, versioned, dependency-checked — see Packaging). Anti-patterns: blocking network calls in initialize (defer to hooks or threads), duplicate NAME s across files (second load swaps the first), absolute paths in configs (store project-relative), per-frame allocations in step (cache in initialize ). Related: Example Plugin walkthrough (conventions), PluginBase Lifecycle (hooks), .zplugin Packaging (distribution), Plugin Manager panel (Editor Manual).

docs.text: VR Plugin Editor and runtime virtual-reality support in plugins/vr_plugin/ ( NAME = "VRPlugin" , VERSION = "1.0.0" , SYSTEM = True in vr_plugin/plug/plugin.py , get_plugin() in vr_plugin/plug/__init__.py ): a runtime core plus an editor dock. plug/plugin.py ( VRPluginBase ) + components/ ( xr_rig.py , xr_locomotion.py , xr_haptics.py , xr_ar.py , xrinter/ ) — session and device management: headset poses feed the scene cameras, controllers appear as tracked input alongside the standard Input API for scripts. vr_dock.py — editor panel: start/stop VR sessions, mirror the headset view into a viewport, device status and per-eye settings. Workflow: open the VR dock, connect the headset, start the session — the game view renders the stereo pair while the desktop viewport keeps the editor camera for staging. Scripts read controller poses through the same Transform/Input conventions as desktop (device-specific bindings surface as buttons and axes). Performance stance: VR doubles the render load (two eyes) — halve render_scale first, then shadow resolution, then PostFX. The profiler's per-stage timings apply per eye; budget 11 ms total, not per eye. Scope note: desktop-first engine with a VR annex, not a VR-native engine — room-scale tracking and guardian flows depend on the OpenVR/OpenXR runtimes installed on the machine. Troubleshooting: headset not found → runtime (SteamVR/monado) not running; black one eye → resolution scale overflow, lower render_scale; drift → tracking loss in the runtime, recenter there. Related: Cameras (stereo pair source), Input API (controller bindings), Profiler, Render Resolution modes.

docs.text: .zplugin Packaging Signed distributable plugin format: one file carrying code, native modules, bundled libraries and a manifest — install by dropping it in, verified before it ever executes. Package anatomy: Manifest: name, version, entry description, dependencies list (other plugins or libraries with versions), optional cython_modules for bundled native builds. Code entries: .py modules loaded through the standard factory convention. Native entries: .pyd / .so / .dll under the _native/ discipline — the verifier rejects unindexed native modules outright. libs/ bundled dependencies activated per plugin, isolated from other plugins' versions. Build tools: tools/build_plugin.py assembles a plain plugin directory; tools/build_zplugin.py compiles native parts (Cython via cythonize when configured), packs the manifest, code, natives and libs into the .zplugin archive. Install and verification flow: Drop the file where the manager scans (or install from the plugin package panel). verify_zplugin_file ( core/foundation/plugins/discovery.py:80 ) validates the manifest, reports missing dependencies by name, and checks the entry index; payload files re-checked by _verify_payload_files (hash mismatch → modified file , unindexed .pyd / .so / .dll outside _native/ rejected). Signatures ( verify_manifest_signature ) verify against config/trusted_keys *.pub files (64-hex ed25519 keys, plus optional trusted_keys_dir ); policy allow_unsigned ( warn default, strict blocks): with no keys configured verification reports no trusted keys configured instead of silently passing. _zplugin_fingerprint ( core/foundation/plugins/ui_registry.py:130 , sha256 + size + mtime) consults the extraction cache — reinstalls of unchanged files cost nothing. Activation resolves dependencies, mounts bundled libs, loads the entry. Updating: bump the manifest version, rebuild, redistribute — the fingerprint changes, the cache re-extracts, dependents re-resolve. Keep NAME stable across versions or configs orphan. The repo ships an example artifact: plugins/mcp_pack-2.1.1.zplugin — inspect it (as an archive) to see a real manifest, native layout and versioning scheme. Troubleshooting: refused unsigned → sign with a trusted key or add the key; missing dependency → install the named package first; stale behavior after rebuild → fingerprint unchanged (mtime granularity), touch or version-bump; native load failure → architecture mismatch (win .pyd / .dll vs linux .so ). Related: Plugin Manager (verification chain), User Plugins guide (what to pack), System Plugins catalog.

In user scripts Input , KeyCode , Vec2/3/4 , Curve , Range , Logger are pre-injected, so imports below are only needed for editor/tooling code — same objects either way. docs.text: Glossary and FAQ Glossary Entity — scene object with UUID, name, parent/children, tags, layer, active toggle. Behavior comes only from components. Component — data + lifecycle hooks ( on_awake/on_start/on_update/on_fixed_update/on_destroy/on_enable/on_disable ) auto-discovered via ComponentRegistry . ScriptComponent — the component that hosts a user .py behavior: script_path + script_fields + hot_reload . Behavior class — first class in the script file declaring a lifecycle/collision/gizmo member or _inspector_buttons ; no base class, constructed with no arguments. Inspector field — annotated class attribute rendered as a widget; values persist per instance in the scene. Play — run mode: scripts load, on_awake / on_start fire, per-frame updates run. Gizmo methods also run outside Play. Hot-reload — mtime-triggered instance recreation during Play preserving Inspector values. Fixed update — physics-clock callback with stable dt ( 0.02 default); render dt is already time-scaled. Prefab ( .zpep ) — saved entity subtree with stable GUIDs; instances remap GUIDs and keep overrides. Cython companion — sibling .pyx auto-built into cache/cython on first import, rebuilt when newer. Time scale — multiplier applied to render dt ; fixed-step dt stays constant. FAQ Script does nothing on Play? The Script field is empty or points at a moved file ( script_path is project-root-relative). Re-pick it; the Check action reports file:line errors. Vec3.rotate missing? Correct — rotation lives on Transform.rotate(Vec3 degrees) . Vec3 offers dot/cross/length/normalized/lerp , not rotate . core.math3d import fails? Import from core.maths.math3d . The Check button suggests exactly this. Edit during Play lost state? Expected: __init__ state resets on reload by design; keep tunable state in Inspector fields and rebuild caches in on_awake / on_start . Ball falls through the floor? Missing collider, Is Trigger without contact handling, or Is Kinematic where solver motion is expected. No sound? clip_path empty/unresolvable, AudioListener missing from the camera entity, or play() called with no AudioSystem in a headless context. First Play is slow with .pyx ? One-time native compile into cache/cython ; later runs reuse it. The Check button validates .pyx without a C compiler.

docs.text: Roadmap, Changelog, License Facts only — everything below is read straight from the repository. License Mozilla Public License 2.0. Copyright (c) 2026 Zarrakun. Full text in LICENSE at the repository root. Requirements (from README.md ) Python 3.13+, PySide6 ≥ 6.6.0, ModernGL ≥ 5.10.0, NumPy ≥ 1.26.0, system OpenAL for audio, bundled Assimp DLL/SO for mesh import. Full list in requirements.txt . OpenGL 4.6 Core Profile. All engine math is numpy.float64 ; float32 conversion happens only at GPU upload. Entry points and tests python main.py — editor. python player.py Scene.zpes — run a scene (default "SampleScene.zpes" ). python build_nuitka.py — Nuitka standalone build (settings in BuildSettings.json ). python setup.py — compiles the 34 engine Cython extensions from core/pyx/*.pyx : _convex_hull , _bvh_build , _raytracing_data , math_helpers , _math_vec , _culling , _transform_batch , _render_utils , _physics_utils , _core_batch , _types , _ecs_batch , _render_batch , _octree_batch , _constraint_batch , _curve_batch , _constraint_update , _physics_sync , _mesh_import , _skinning , _ik , _physbone , _audio_dsp , _raycast , _shadow_batch , _scene_query , _render_collect , _math_mat4 , _vr_batch , _nav_batch , _splat_sort , _gs_volume , _sky_astro (plus _shader_parse sources). Windows default toolchain is the auto-downloaded compact MinGW-w64. Smoke tests in tests/smoke/ : test_scripting , test_script_inspector , test_script_cython , test_engine_embed , test_relpaths , test_import_materials , test_mesh_import_persist , test_ik_numeric , test_blendshapes , test_compression_async , test_digest_dedup , test_duplicate_skinned , test_embed2 , test_embed_outside , test_prop_picker , test_soft_remote , plus tests/libs/test_library_packs.py . Changelog and roadmap No CHANGELOG.md ships with the repository: the git history is the change record. The scripting contract source of truth is docs/scripting.md in the engine repo. Verifiable direction from the code (not promises): gameplay-side networking is stubs ( host / connect / send / broadcast / poll awaiting a transport; NetworkIdentity is a stub component), while ECS, editor, rendering, physics, audio, GUI, prefabs, scripting hot-reload and user Cython companions are implemented and covered by the smoke tests above.

docs.text: Atmosphere Physical sky LUT: Atmosphere ( core/components/rendering/environment/atmosp/component.py:11-163 ), singleton-per-scene via Atmosphere.for_scene(scene) . Home · Section index Overview Computes a transmittance/multi-scatter LUT ( atmosp/compute.py , AtmosphereLutMixin ); _resolution_scale scales the LUT. Only the first enabled instance per scene is used ( for_scene ). All fields are underscore-prefixed in serialization. Properties name type default description _intensity slider (1–60) 20.0 Sky gain ( component.py:20,42 ). _sun_intensity slider (0–10) 1.0 Sun disk gain ( component.py:22,43 ). _resolution_scale slider (0.25–1) 1.0 LUT resolution ( component.py:23,44 ). _ozone_factor slider (0–3) 1.0 Ozone absorption ( component.py:24,45 ). _aerosol_scale slider (0–5) 1.0 Aerosols/Mie amount ( component.py:25,46 ). _rayleigh_scale slider (0–3) 1.0 Rayleigh amount ( component.py:26,47 ). _mie_anisotropy slider (0–0.95) 0.76 Mie g ( component.py:27,48 ). _mie_albedo slider (0–1) 0.9 Mie albedo ( component.py:28,49 ). _ground_albedo slider (0–1) 0.3 Ground bounce ( component.py:29,50 ). _multiscatter_strength slider (0–2) 1.0 Multi-scatter gain ( component.py:30,51 ). _horizon_haze slider (0–2) 0.4 Horizon haze ( component.py:31,52 ). _planet_radius slider km (6000–6500) 6360.0 Planet radius ( component.py:32,53 ). _atmosphere_height slider km (20–120) 60.0 Top height ( component.py:33,54 ). _camera_height_m slider m (0–8000) 20.0 Reference eye height ( component.py:34,55 ). _sun_angular_radius slider deg (0.05–1) 0.27 Sun size ( component.py:35,56 ). _sun_limb_darkening slider (0–1) 0.7 Limb darkening ( component.py:36,57 ). _sun_convergence slider (0–1) 0.5 Edge softness ( component.py:37,58 ). _color_temperature slider K (2000–20000) 5778.0 Sun blackbody ( component.py:38,59 ). ## Usage in Editor Single Atmosphere per scene. Lower _rayleigh_scale for alien skies, raise _aerosol_scale / _horizon_haze for dusty sunsets. ## Usage in Code atmo = Atmosphere.for_scene(scene) atmo._sun_intensity = 1.4 atmo._rayleigh_scale = 0.8 Related pages Procedural Sky , Skybox , Directional Light Verified against core/components/rendering/environment/atmosp/component.py:16-60,84-163

docs.text: Camera Scene camera: Camera component ( core/components/rendering/cameras/camera.py ) with perspective/orthographic projection, depth ordering and native/custom render size. docs.text: Overview Forward OpenGL renderer: Renderer facade in core/renderer/renderer.py draws the scene into the viewport FBO in opaque then transparent phases. Home · Section index Overview ZarinEngine uses a forward renderer built on moderngl. Entry context is created in main.py : QSurfaceFormat , OpenGL 4.6 Core profile, depth buffer 24, swap interval from rendering.vsync ( 0 off / 1 on). Renderer composes mixins: config, programs, voxel, object-fx, framebuffers, water, uniforms, skinned, collector, geometry cache, outline, gizmo, icon, cubemap, post, scene ( core/renderer/renderer.py:56 ). Render modes are RenderMode.SHADED / SHADED_WIREFRAME / FLAT ( core/renderer/types.py ). Default caps: _max_lights = 8 , ambient [0.26, 0.28, 0.34] , selection outline [0.8, 0.5, 0.1, 1.0] thickness 0.03 ( core/renderer/renderer.py:90-114 ). Properties name type default description rendering.vsync bool (global config) True Swap interval 1 on / 0 off ( main.py:212 ). rendering.max_lights int (global config) 8 Size of u_lights[] uniform array ( core/renderer/rconfig/config_state.py:20 ). rendering.ambient vec3 (global config) [0.26, 0.28, 0.34] Fallback ambient ( core/renderer/renderer.py:112 ). render_mode RenderMode SHADED Shaded / shaded+wireframe / flat ( core/renderer/types.py ). ## Usage in Editor Viewport renders the active scene with the scene camera; grid, gizmos and outline are editor-only passes. docs.text: Pipeline Forward pipeline in SceneRendererMixin.render_scene : collect snapshot → shadow maps → opaque phase → transparent phase → environment (sky/water/clouds) → editor overlays. Home · Section index Overview render_scene(scene, view_mat, proj_mat, cam_pos, viewport_w, viewport_h, ...) ( core/renderer/scenev/mixin.py:24 ) applies _render_scale to get render size, collects a _RenderSnapshot (lights, dir_light , sky/cloud/water components, renderable entries), renders shadow maps via ShadowRenderer , then calls _scenev_render_forward_phases(opaque, transparent, ...) ( core/renderer/scenev/forward.py:19 ). Transparent phase enables SRC_ALPHA, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA blending with depth_mask = False . Specialized passes: WaterPassMixin , VoxelPassMixin , SkinnedPassMixin , cubemap pass for dynamic reflections, GizmoPassMixin / IconPassMixin / OutlinePassMixin for the editor. docs.text: PostFX Stack Post-effects run in component order after the main scene pass. Each effect is a GraphicsEffect component with an enable toggle and its own Inspector fields. One page per effect: Bloom Blur Chromatic Aberration Color Grading Depth of Field Directional Blur Dithering Edge Detection Film Grain Fog FSR2 FXAA Glitch God Rays Hatching Kuwahara Lens Distortion Lens Flares Motion Blur Panini Pixelate Quantize Radial Blur Scanlines Sharpen Sobel SSAO SSR SVGF Vignette Watercolor Recipes: clean 3D (FXAA, Color Grading, Vignette), cinematic (Bloom, Depth of Field, Film Grain, Color Grading), retro (Pixelate, Scanlines, Dithering), horror (Fog, Vignette, Chromatic Aberration, Sharpen).

docs.text: Shadows Shadow-map system: ShadowRenderer ( core/renderer/shadows/renderer.py , passes.py:183 ) plus per-type quality owners DirectionalShadow / PointShadow / SpotShadow / AreaShadow . Home · Section index Overview render_shadow_pass(...) renders renderable_shadow casters into per-light maps: CSM for directional ( shadows/csm.py ), cube/dual maps for point ( shadows/point_spot.py ), perspective for spot, multi-sample for area ( shadows/area.py ), cookies for Projector ( shadows/projector.py ). Without an active owner component of a type, that type's shadows are disabled (headers in directional_shadow.py:7-9 , point_shadow.py:7-9 , spot_shadow.py:7-9 , area_shadow.py:7-9 ). Per-receiver flags: MeshRenderer.cast_shadows / receive_shadows . Properties name type default description DirectionalShadow._shadow_resolution int slider 256–4096 4096 Sun map size ( directional_shadow.py:33,45 ). DirectionalShadow._shadow_distance float slider 1–500 50.0 CSM range ( directional_shadow.py:35,46 ). DirectionalShadow._cascade_count int slider 1–4 4 Cascade count ( directional_shadow.py:37,58 ). DirectionalShadow._cascade_splits split gradient [0.05, 0.13, 0.3] Cascade boundaries for 4 cascades ( directional_shadow.py:18,39,47 ). PointShadow._shadow_resolution int slider 128–2048 512 Point map size ( point_shadow.py:31,37 ). SpotShadow._shadow_resolution int slider 128–2048 1024 Spot map size ( spot_shadow.py:31,37 ). AreaShadow._shadow_resolution int slider 128–2048 512 Area map size ( area_shadow.py:31,37 ). Light.cast_shadows bool True Per-light toggle (see light pages). ## Usage in Editor Add exactly one owner per type you use (e.g. Directional Shadow). Raise Resolution for crisp edges, shorten Shadow Distance to concentrate CSM texels, use 2–3 cascades for small scenes and 4 for open worlds. ## Usage in Code ds = entity.get_component(DirectionalShadow) ds._shadow_resolution = 2048 ds._shadow_distance = 120.0 Related pages Light , Directional Light , Point Light , Spot Light , Area Light , Mesh Renderer Verified against core/renderer/shadows/passes.py:59,183 core/renderer/shadows/csm.py , point_spot.py , area.py , projector.py:28 core/components/rendering/environment/directional_shadow.py:28-48 core/components/rendering/environment/point_shadow.py:26-37 core/components/rendering/environment/spot_shadow.py:26-37 core/components/rendering/environment/area_shadow.py:26-37

docs.text: Cython in Scripts Heavy computations move to a Cython module next to the plain script — no manual build steps, no polluted script folders. Setup: Project → Create → Cython Script creates fast_sum.pyx with a working template. A plain script in the same folder writes import fast_sum . Before import, the engine prepares the script folder on the module search path, then on first import compiles the extension into cache/cython automatically. On Windows the bundled MinGW toolchain is discovered by the engine itself. import move_fast class Mover: speed: float = 5.0 def on_update(self, dt): step = move_fast.clamp_step(self.speed * dt, 0.0, 1.0) t = self._entity.transform if t: t.translate(Vec3(0.0, 0.0, step)) cpdef double clamp_step(double value, double lo, double hi): if value < lo: return lo if value > hi: return hi return value Rules and mechanics: The module name is top-level: import foo where foo.pyx sits next to the script. Names must be unique within the project. A neighboring foo.pxd declaration file is tracked for rebuilds too. Rebuilds are automatic when the .pyx (or .pxd ) is newer than the cached build. Artifacts live in cache/cython under build/<dirhash16>/<fingerprint12> (directory hash + 12-hex source fingerprint over .pyx , neighboring .pxd , Cython version and toolchain); only the last 3 builds per script folder are kept. The script folder stays clean. Editing .pyx during Play triggers a script hot-reload as usual. The Check button validates .pyx without a C compiler (Cython parsing and typing only). The full native build happens lazily on first import. If no compiler is found, the console shows an actionable error and the script keeps working on the previous working build — iteration never hard-blocks on toolchain setup. Keep the Python/Cython boundary typed ( cpdef , typed locals) and batch calls: one call processing an array beats per-element calls across the boundary. When to reach for it: per-frame math over many elements (crowds, particles logic, procedural deformation), tight loops the profiler attributes to a script, and numeric kernels. Game flow, input and orchestration stay in plain Python. Troubleshooting: stale results → touch the .pyx (mtime drives rebuilds); import errors → module name collision within the project, rename uniquely; slow first Play → that is the one-time compile, later runs reuse cache/cython .

docs.text: Script Examples Copy-paste behaviors. All run as-is: create a Python Script asset, replace its content, attach to an entity, press Play. Rotator — spins around Y using the frame delta: from core.maths.math3d import Vec3 class Rotator: speed: float = 90.0 def on_update(self, dt): t = self._entity.get_component_by_name("Transform") if t: t.rotate(Vec3(0.0, self.speed * dt, 0.0)) Mover — constant forward motion with an Inspector slider: from typing import Annotated from core.maths.math3d import Vec3 class Mover: speed: Annotated[float, Range(0.0, 20.0)] = 5.0 def on_update(self, dt): t = self._entity.transform if t: t.translate(Vec3(0.0, 0.0, self.speed * dt)) Keyboard driver — WASD movement plus sprint on Shift: from core.maths.math3d import Vec3 class Driver: speed: float = 6.0 sprint: float = 10.0 def on_update(self, dt): v = Vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0) if Input.GetKey(KeyCode.W): v = v + Vec3(0.0, 0.0, 1.0) if Input.GetKey(KeyCode.S): v = v + Vec3(0.0, 0.0, -1.0) if Input.GetKey(KeyCode.A): v = v + Vec3(-1.0, 0.0, 0.0) if Input.GetKey(KeyCode.D): v = v + Vec3(1.0, 0.0, 0.0) rate = self.sprint if (Input.GetKey(KeyCode.LEFT_SHIFT) or Input.GetKey(KeyCode.RIGHT_SHIFT)) else self.speed t = self._entity.transform if t and v.length() > 0.0: t.translate(v.normalized() * rate * dt) Patrol — waypoint ping-pong with an enum mode and a cached Transform: from enum import Enum from core.maths.math3d import Vec3 class PatrolMode(Enum): PINGPONG = 0 LOOP = 1 class Patrol: mode: PatrolMode = PatrolMode.PINGPONG speed: float = 3.0 distance: float = 8.0 def on_awake(self): self.t = self._entity.transform self.home = Vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0) self.dir = 1.0 if self.t: self.home = self.t.position def on_update(self, dt): if not self.t: return step = self.speed * self.dir * dt self.t.translate(Vec3(step, 0.0, 0.0)) walked = self.t.position.x - self.home.x if self.mode == PatrolMode.LOOP: if walked > self.distance or walked < 0.0: self.t.position = Vec3(self.home.x, self.t.position.y, self.t.position.z) else: if walked > self.distance or walked < 0.0: self.dir = -self.dir Follower — chase an Entity picked in the Inspector: from core.maths.math3d import Vec3 class Follower: target: 'Entity' = None speed: float = 4.0 stop_at: float = 1.5 def on_update(self, dt): if not self.target: return t = self._entity.transform goal = self.target.transform if not t or not goal: return delta = goal.position - t.position dist = delta.length() if dist > self.stop_at: t.translate(delta.normalized() * self.speed * dt) Hit counter — collision callbacks with impact force and an Inspector button: class HitCounter: hits: int = 0 last_force: float = 0.0 _inspector_buttons = [("reset", "Reset")] def on_collision_enter(self, other_id, force): self.hits = self.hits + 1 self.last_force = force def reset(self): self.hits = 0 self.last_force = 0.0 Physics kick — impulse on key press for an entity with Rigidbody: from core.maths.math3d import Vec3 class Kicker: impulse: float = 5.0 def on_update(self, dt): if Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.SPACE): rb = self._entity.get_component_by_name("Rigidbody") if rb: rb.add_impulse(Vec3(0.0, self.impulse, 0.0)) Countdown spawner — timed logic with enable/disable safety: class Spawner: interval: float = 2.0 active: bool = True def on_awake(self): self.clock = 0.0 self.count = 0 def on_update(self, dt): if not self.active: return self.clock = self.clock + dt if self.clock >= self.interval: self.clock = 0.0 self.count = self.count + 1 Logger.info("spawn tick") def on_disable(self): self.clock = 0.0

docs.text: Hot Reload A script file can be edited while Play is running. The change is picked up on the next frame: the instance is recreated, Inspector values are preserved, and on_awake / on_start run again. Instance state from __init__ is reset, like a recompilation in Unity. Reload pipeline: The engine compares the file modification time before each on_update / on_fixed_update . A newer mtime starts a reload. The file is re-validated (same checks as the Check button). On errors a single consolidated console message Script '...' has N error(s): is written per file version, and the previous working instance keeps running. On success the module re-executes with the injected API, the behavior class is re-resolved, and a fresh instance is constructed. Inspector field values are re-applied onto the new instance, then on_awake and on_start run again. What survives: Inspector-tuned values, the component wiring, the entity hierarchy. What resets: anything assigned in __init__ or built up in callbacks (timers, caches, spawned handles) — rebuild it in on_awake / on_start if the behavior must continue seamlessly. The Check button validates without Play in three stages: syntax parse with file:line positions, core.* import resolution (including the hint to use core.maths.math3d instead of core.math3d ), and a full trial execution catching runtime import errors such as circular imports. Control: the hot_reload flag on ScriptComponent (default True ). Set False to freeze the instance for the session — useful when debugging native-side state or comparing against a fixed baseline. Workflow tips: keep Play running and iterate on feel (speeds, curves, timings) with an external editor; the tuned Inspector values persist across reloads, so save the scene when the feel is right. For structural refactors (renamed fields, new buttons) expect one clean reload cycle and re-check the Inspector. Troubleshooting: changes ignored → the file did not save (mtime unchanged) or hot_reload is off; old behavior persists with errors → fix the reported file:line entries, the last working build stays live meanwhile; fields reset → the annotation was renamed, the old stored value has no target.

docs.text: Input and Math API These names are injected into every user script module automatically, so importing them is optional. An explicit import with the same name in the script takes priority over the injection. Injected names: Input , KeyCode , Vec2 , Vec3 , Vec4 , Curve , Range , Logger . Keyboard and mouse: Input.GetKey(code) — held this frame; Input.GetKeyDown(code) — pressed this frame; Input.GetKeyUp(code) — released this frame. Codes come from KeyCode ( KeyCode.W , KeyCode.SPACE , KeyCode.LEFT_SHIFT / KeyCode.RIGHT_SHIFT , arrows, digits and more). Input.GetMouseButton(i) , GetMouseButtonDown(i) , GetMouseButtonUp(i) — button index state. Input.GetButton(name) , GetButtonDown(name) , GetButtonUp(name) — named action buttons. Input.GetAxis(name) , Input.GetAxisRaw(name) — smoothed vs raw axes such as "Horizontal" . Input.mousePosition — cursor in screen space; Input.deltaTime — scaled frame time; Input.cursorLocked / Input.cursorVisible — pointer capture state. Math: Vec2 , Vec3 , Vec4 — full vector math (add, scale, dot, cross, length, normalized, lerp) backed by numpy.float64 ; the GPU downgrade to float32 happens only on upload. Quat , Mat4 — import from core.maths.math3d for rotations and matrices (slerp, look_at, perspective helpers live there with numba acceleration). Curve — keyframed response curves edited in the Inspector and evaluated at runtime for falloff, easing and throttle shapes. Range — slider metadata for Inspector fields (see Inspector Fields). Logger — Logger.info/warning/error with timestamps; errors include tracebacks and reach the console panel. Frame-rate independence: always multiply motion by dt (or use Input.deltaTime ); fixed-step logic belongs in on_fixed_update with its stable step. class Player: speed: float = 6.0 def on_update(self, dt): step = self.speed * dt t = self._entity.transform if Input.GetKey(KeyCode.W): t.translate(Vec3(0.0, 0.0, step)) if Input.GetKey(KeyCode.S): t.translate(Vec3(0.0, 0.0, -step)) if Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.SPACE): Logger.info("jump pressed") class Looker: sensitivity: float = 2.0 def on_update(self, dt): x = Input.GetAxis("Horizontal") t = self._entity.transform if t and x != 0.0: t.rotate(Vec3(0.0, x * self.sensitivity * dt, 0.0)) Cursor pattern for fly cameras: lock on right-mouse hold, release on up — drive Input.cursorLocked from the mouse-button callbacks in on_update . Axes such as "Horizontal" exist only after bindings are loaded ( Input.LoadProjectBindings at startup) or an explicit Input.DefineAxis("Horizontal", positive=[KeyCode.D], negative=[KeyCode.A]) . An undefined axis name makes GetAxis / GetAxisRaw return 0.0 , so the Looker above stays still until the axis is defined — define it in project setup before relying on it (see Input overview).

docs.text: Inspector Fields and Range Annotated class attributes automatically appear in the Inspector, and their values are stored in the scene ( .zpes ). Class-level defaults become the initial values; per-instance edits override them without touching the .py file. Private names starting with _ are skipped, except the special _inspector_buttons . from enum import Enum from typing import Annotated from core.maths.math3d import Vec3 from core.foundation.curve import Curve class Mode(Enum): IDLE = 0 PATROL = 1 class Enemy: speed: Annotated[float, Range(0.0, 10.0)] = 5.0 health: int = 100 title: str = "grunt" active: bool = True offset: Vec3 = Vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0) mode: Mode = Mode.PATROL falloff: Curve = Curve() target: 'Entity' = None _inspector_buttons = [("explode", "Explode")] def explode(self): self.health = 0 Annotation Inspector widget Stored as float Number field float int Integer field int bool Checkbox bool str Text field string Annotated[float, Range(min, max[, step])] Float slider, default step 0.01 float clamped to range Annotated[int, Range(min, max)] Integer slider, default step 1 int clamped to range Vec2 / Vec3 / Vec4 Vector fields float components Enum subclass Dropdown of member names enum value 'Entity' Entity picker UUID; the live object is passed to the script Curve Curve editor keyframe set Details: Range is Range(min_value=0.0, max_value=1.0, step=None) . A plain [min, max] or (min, max[, step]) sequence in Annotated metadata works identically. Entity picker stores the target UUID in the scene and resolves the live object before each call — safe across renames, unlike name-based lookup. Resource-typed fields (mesh, material, texture, audio, prefab, scene, physics material) reuse the built-in picker dialogs and their file filters: models *.obj *.fbx *.stl *.gltf *.glb *.usdz *.dae *.3ds *.blend , materials *.zpem *.mat , images *.png *.jpg *.jpeg *.bmp *.tga *.tif *.tiff *.webp *.hdr *.exr *.dds *.svg , audio *.wav *.mp3 *.ogg *.flac *.aiff *.m4a , scripts *.py , prefabs *.zpep , scenes *.zpes , animation clips and controllers, physics materials *.zphysmat . _inspector_buttons = [(method_name, label), ...] renders buttons that invoke the method on the live Play instance (or the editor instance outside Play) — handy for test triggers like explode, reset or spawn. The component header shows an immutable Script field with the file display name: click reveals the file in the Project panel, the ... button opens the built-in script editor. Changing the file rebuilds the field list; values for surviving names are kept. Hot-reload re-applies Inspector values onto the recreated instance, so tuning survives code edits. Guidance: expose designers' knobs (speeds, counts, toggles) as fields, keep internal caches ( self._cache , cooldowns) as plain un-annotated attributes set in on_awake .

docs.text: Lifecycle Callbacks Every callback is optional. Define only what the behavior needs; the engine caches per-method lookups and skips missing ones without cost. Method Short alias Signature When it runs on_awake awake () Once when Play starts, before on_start ; use for caches and peer lookups on_start start () Once when Play starts; use for initial state and first actions on_update update (dt) Every rendered frame in scene order; dt already scaled by time scale on_fixed_update fixed_update (dt) Every physics step with stable dt ( 0.02 default); forces and movement here on_enable enable () When the entity becomes active ( entity.active = True ) on_disable disable () When the entity becomes inactive; stop loops and sounds here on_collision_enter — (other_id) or (other_id, force) Contact starts on_collision_stay — (other_id) or (other_id, force) Contact continues on_collision_exit — (other_id) or (other_id, force) Contact ends on_destroy destroy () Component removed or scene unloaded; release resources here gizmo_lines — () -> list Editor gizmo lines, runs outside Play too gizmo_meshes — () -> list Editor gizmo meshes, runs outside Play too Call order at Play start: on_awake for every scripted component, then on_start for every scripted component. Do not assume sibling start order — fetch peers lazily or in on_update guards. dt semantics: render dt stretches with slow motion and pause (time scale 0 freezes updates); fixed dt stays constant so physics and its scripts stay deterministic. Collision dispatch: the solver reports contacts to the physics layer, which maps solver bodies to entity ids and invokes callbacks. Arity is measured once from the signature — two parameters receive (other_id: str, force: float) , one parameter receives just other_id . Resolve the other entity inside the callback only if needed; id comparison is cheaper. Enable/disable: toggling entity.active fires on_disable / on_enable on all components of that entity, scripts included. Disabling mid-Play pauses that behavior without destroying its instance state. Destroy cases: removing the ScriptComponent in the editor, deleting the entity, unloading the scene, or stopping Play. Hot-reload recreates the instance but preserves Inspector field values and re-runs on_awake / on_start . Exceptions: any error in any callback is caught and logged as Script ... error ... with a traceback naming the script and method. The frame, the physics step and the remaining components continue. class Fighter: health: int = 100 def on_awake(self): self.hits = 0 self.body = self._entity.get_component_by_name("Rigidbody") def on_start(self): self.alive = True def on_update(self, dt): if self.health <= 0 and self.alive: self.alive = False self._entity.active = False def on_fixed_update(self, dt): if self.body and self.health <= 0: self.body.velocity = Vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0) def on_collision_enter(self, other_id, force): self.hits = self.hits + 1 self.health = self.health - int(force) def on_destroy(self): self.hits = 0 self.body = None

docs.text: Scripting Overview Entity behaviors in ZarinEngine are plain .py files with a behavior class. No base class, no registration boilerplate, no build step — the file itself is the asset. End-to-end flow: Project → Create → Python Script creates the file inside the project folder. Keep scripts next to the content that uses them; sibling imports (including Cython modules) resolve from the script folder automatically. Select an entity, Inspector → Add Component → Scripts , pick the file in the Script field. Annotated class attributes instantly become Inspector widgets. Tune values in the Inspector — they are stored in the scene ( .zpes ), not in the .py file, so one script drives many tuned instances. Press Play . The engine loads the class, instantiates it with no arguments, assigns self._entity , and calls on_awake then on_start . How it works inside: The engine finds the first class in alphabetical attribute order ( dir() order, not definition order) that declares at least one lifecycle callback, collision callback, gizmo method, or _inspector_buttons . Inheritance is not required; the constructor must take no arguments. Short names are full aliases: update = on_update , start = on_start , and so on for awake, fixed_update, destroy, enable, disable. If both variants are defined, the on_* version wins. One entity can hold several ScriptComponent instances ( _allow_multiple = True ): movement, health and visuals as separate scripts on one object. An exception inside any callback never crashes the game: it is written to the console with the script and method name, and the frame continues with the next component. script_path is stored relative to the project root, so scenes and scripts move between machines cleanly. Execution context: on_update(dt) runs in scene order every rendered frame with dt already multiplied by the time scale; on_fixed_update(dt) runs on the physics clock with a stable step ( 0.02 default). Collision callbacks arrive from the physics dispatch, not the ECS loop, with the other entity id and optionally the impact force. Gizmo methods ( gizmo_lines , gizmo_meshes ) execute in the editor even outside Play for custom handles and debug drawing. Performance guidance: scripts are Python and run per frame — keep on_update lean, cache component lookups in on_start instead of fetching by name every frame, and move number-crunching into Cython modules (see Cython in Scripts). Subpages: Lifecycle Callbacks — every method, signature and call order. Inspector Fields and Range — annotations to widgets, Entity pickers, buttons. Input and Math API — injected names, keys, axes, vectors, curves. Hot Reload — editing scripts during Play. Cython in Scripts — compiled helpers with zero manual builds. ScriptComponent — paths, flags, class resolution, Check. Script Examples — copy-paste behaviors.

docs.text: ScriptComponent ScriptComponent is the engine side of user scripts: it loads the .py file, builds Inspector fields from the class, forwards lifecycle calls, stores field values in the scene, and validates on demand. Component facts: script_path is stored relative to the project root, so scenes are portable. A relative path that does not resolve directly is retried against the project root; absolute paths resolve as-is. hot_reload defaults to True . Several ScriptComponent instances may live on one entity ( _allow_multiple = True ). The Inspector header shows the file display name (base name without extension) with a reveal action and an editor button; a second header lists the discovered script variables. Class resolution, in order: Modification-time short-circuit: unchanged mtime reuses the cached class with zero work. Import preparation: the script folder joins the module search so sibling .py and compiled Cython modules resolve. Error collection: syntax parse, core.* import checks, trial execution. On errors one consolidated Script '...' has N error(s): message is logged per file version, the old instance is dropped, and no fields render until the file is fixed. Module execution with the injected API ( Input , KeyCode , Vec2/3/4 , Curve , Range , Logger ). Class pick: the first class in alphabetical attribute order ( dir() order, not definition order) that declares at least one lifecycle callback, collision callback, gizmo method, or _inspector_buttons . Instantiated with no arguments; self._entity is assigned before every call. Method caching: bound methods per canonical name with fast flags for on_update / on_fixed_update ; collision arities measured once via signature inspection; field hints cached until the file changes. Serialization: script_path and the script_fields dict persist in .zpes , so tuned instances survive reloads, prefabs and version control. hot_reload (default True ) is a runtime-only flag and is not serialized. The Check action runs step 3 on demand and reports file:line: message rows — including the core.maths.math3d vs core.math3d hint and circular-import failures — so broken scripts are diagnosed without pressing Play. Multiple instances on one entity each keep an independent module state, instance and field set; they reload independently. Cross-script communication goes through the entity ( get_component by sibling script is resolved via its component, or shared state on the entity).
